Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the failing test does:
  - It creates a new instance encoder: Encoder enc = new Base64().
  - For each known input byte[] (BYTES[i]), it expects enc.encode(binary) to equal the corresponding Base64-encoded string bytes (utf8(STRINGS[i])) without any line breaks.
  - Assertion fails when the encoder output includes extra characters not present in STRINGS[i].

- Reported behavior:
  - The instance method new Base64().encode() appends CRLF and chunks results into 76-character lines, whereas Commons-Codec 1.3 did not. The static Base64.encodeBase64() still behaves correctly; only the instance encode() is affected.

- Where the behavior comes from in the code:
  - Base64() constructor delegates to Base64(boolean): 
    - Base64() -> this(false) [lines 224–226]
    - Base64(boolean) -> this(CHUNK_SIZE, CHUNK_SEPARATOR, urlSafe) [lines 243–245]
  - CHUNK_SIZE is 76 and CHUNK_SEPARATOR is "\r\n" [lines 68, 79].
  - Base64(int, byte[], boolean) uses the provided separator to enable chunking unless the separator is null. If lineSeparator is null, chunking is disabled by forcing lineLength=0 [lines 320–339].
  - The encoder implementation injects line separators:
    - During streaming: after every 76 encoded chars (currentLinePos >= lineLength), it copies lineSeparator into the output [lines 505–509].
    - At EOF: if any output and lineLength > 0, it appends a final lineSeparator [lines 484–487].
  - The instance encode(Object)/encode(byte[]) path used by the test goes through this chunking behavior by default:
    - encode(Object) just delegates to encode(byte[]) [lines 902–907].
    - encode(byte[]) sets up buffer using lineLength and lineSeparator, then calls the streaming encode(..) which does the chunking and final CRLF append [lines 928–949 and 452–513].

- Why the test fails:
  - The test expects unchunked Base64 output (as in Codec 1.3), but new Base64() now defaults to chunking with a CRLF every 76 characters and a trailing CRLF at EOF.
  - This changes the byte[] returned by enc.encode(binary), making it different from the expected STRINGS[i] bytes, causing the assertion to fail.

- Root cause:
  - A behavioral change in the default Base64() constructor: it enables chunking by default via CHUNK_SIZE and CHUNK_SEPARATOR, whereas Commons-Codec 1.3’s instance encoder did not chunk by default.
  - Consequently, encode() now appends CRLFs (both during encoding and at the end), breaking compatibility with the expected unchunked output checked in the test.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
